title: Typed layer features
description: What the typed API offers on top of the JSON layer: values that cannot be wrong, outcomes only where time can refuse to answer, and no order without rules.

entities.name: Values that are valid by construction
entities.description: A typed value always names something that exists.
entities.behavior: Constructors are internal; values come from Of, TryOf, Parse, FromJson, the From… interop methods and operations. Of throws ArgumentOutOfRangeException naming the field for 30 February, month 13, hour 25 or second 60; TryOf, Parse and FromJson return the same refusal as an outcome. Interval.Of throws ArgumentException for a reversed interval or one with no point. AtOffset throws for an offset beyond ±18:00, and InZone for a name that is not an IANA zone name.
entities.outcome: Code that holds a CivilDate never has to ask whether it is a real day.
constraints: Years are BigInteger: year 275760 and year -500 are valid dates.
A typed value holds only the everyday shapes; a value with properties the type does not hold is refused, not trimmed.

entities.name: Outcomes only where time can refuse to answer
entities.description: Total operations return plain values; partial ones return Outcome<T>.
entities.behavior: AddDays, AddWeeks, wall-clock additions, DaysUntil, Until, Add(PosixSeconds), ToInstant, Contains and Overlaps return values. AddMonths(n), AddYears(n), Add(Period), Resolve, InZone(id, ctx), Add(ElapsedSeconds), TemporalContext.Compare and the To… interop methods return Outcome<T>: an abstract record with the nested sealed records Unique, Multiple (ascending), None, Unsupported and Invalid, each with its Diagnostics. A total operation whose JSON-layer call ever failed would throw InvalidOperationException, since that would be a library bug.
entities.outcome: Every Outcome in the caller's code marks a question that can have no answer, or several, and the compiler makes the caller look.
constraints: C# does not know the five cases are all there are, so a switch expression needs a final _ => arm.
Outcome.ToString() is the value's text for Unique, otherwise the status and the codes, such as none (month-end).

entities.name: Outcome helpers that never pick an answer
entities.description: Getting a value out of an outcome never chooses among several.
entities.behavior: TryGetUnique is true only for Unique; UniqueOr returns the fallback for anything else; Single throws OutcomeException with the status and diagnostics for anything but Unique. Diagnostics has Codes, Has(code) and readable text.
entities.outcome: Both instants of a DST overlap stay visible until the caller chooses a policy.

entities.name: Total policy overloads accept only Constrain
entities.description: A policy argument cannot change a method's return type.
entities.behavior: AddMonths(n, MonthEnd) and AddYears(n, MonthEnd) on CivilDate, and AddMonths(n, MonthEnd) on CivilDateTime, return a plain value clamped to the month's last day. Passing MonthEnd.Reject throws ArgumentException; the rejecting form is the overload without a policy.
entities.outcome: Clamping happens only where the caller wrote MonthEnd.Constrain.
constraints: Add(Period, MonthEnd) returns an Outcome and accepts both policies.

entities.name: No order for zoned values without rules
entities.description: Zoned intentions are ordered only through a context, and the answer can be several orderings.
entities.behavior: ZonedIntent has no CompareTo and no comparison operators. TemporalContext.Compare resolves both sides with ResolutionPolicy.Strict and compares every pair of candidates. One ordering is Unique; more than one is Multiple with an ambiguous diagnostic, as for 01:30 and 01:45 on the night New York's clocks go back. A side that does not resolve passes its outcome on.
entities.outcome: Nobody sorts meetings by a guess about which side of an overlap was meant.
constraints: TemporalContext holds the rules once; there is no default or ambient context.

entities.name: Representation equality
entities.description: Two typed values are equal when their JSON is the same.
entities.behavior: Every value is an immutable sealed record, so == compares what it holds. CivilTime remembers whether a second was given: 09:30 and 09:30:00 are not equal, though CompareTo puts them level. Outcomes are equal when their case, values and diagnostics are. [DebuggerDisplay] shows CivilDate(2026-11-05).
entities.outcome: Values can be keys in dictionaries and sets, and round-trip through JSON unchanged.
constraints: Sameness in meaning (the same instant written two ways) is not equality.

entities.name: ToString is the text form
entities.description: Each value prints as the text Parse reads back.
entities.behavior: ToString() formats the value's JSON with TextForm.Format. A value with no text form, such as a period with mixed signs, prints its JSON instead. PosixSeconds and ElapsedSeconds print a display string that cannot be parsed: a decimal when the fraction terminates (3600.75 s (POSIX)), otherwise a fraction (1/3 s (POSIX)).
entities.outcome: Logs and test output show 2026-11-05, P1M or [2026-11-01, 2026-12-01), never a type name.
constraints: Only start-end intervals of dates or instants have a text form.
